newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Heineken H1 net up six pct, issues profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Heineken H1 net up six pct, issues profit warning.

text.p: Dutch brewing giant Heineken NV posted first half net profit of 297 million guilders ($175.1 million) on Friday, below analysts' expectations, and added to investors' disappointment with a profit warning.
Heineken shares plunged 32.70 guilders, or nine percent on the news as investors signalled their disapproval.
Heineken said it expected 1996 full-year net profit to be "somewhat" lower than 1995's 664 million guilders.
"Heineken does not expect the beer markets in Europe to grow, which will lead to increasing pressure on margins," the company said in a statement.
It added fine summer weather in 1995 meant sales volume in Europe seemed to be lower in 1996.

The group posted a 20.1 percent increase in turnover to 5.92 billion guilders, and a 7.7 percent increase in trading profit to 464 million. Net profit per share rose to 5.92 guilders from 5.59 in the same year ago period.
Heineken announced an unchanged interim dividend of 1.50 guilders per share.
